title: Live Spatial Data Connector: Feeds on a Map
description: Connect a public GeoJSON or CSV feed with the Live Spatial Data Connector and watch it render on a map — refresh re-reads the source. Free, in-browser.
summary_sentence: Data is fetched directly by the browser when you connect or refresh; CORS must allow access.
quick_answer: Fetch a compatible GeoJSON Feature or FeatureCollection, or a CSV with latitude and longitude headers, directly in the browser. Refresh is manual; the endpoint receives the request and its CORS rules apply.

popular_table.note: Honest limits: the fetch happens in your browser, so the endpoint must allow cross-origin access (CORS) — many public feeds do, some do not, and the tool cannot (and should not) sneak around a publisher who said no.

faq: Does MapBench store the feed or its data?
No. Your browser requests the endpoint directly and renders what returns; nothing is proxied through or kept on a MapBench server. Close the tab and the connection is gone.
What kinds of feeds work best?

Small-to-medium GeoJSON FeatureCollections and tidy CSVs with clear latitude/longitude columns. A national dataset with a million features will make any browser sweat — use a bounded or summarised endpoint where the publisher offers one.
Can I connect a private or key-protected API?
The browser makes a direct fetch and provides no dedicated credential controls. Avoid placing secrets in URLs; the endpoint and browser history may expose them.
How do I know the data is current?
Read the feed's own timestamps — good feeds carry generated-at or per-feature times. The connector renders faithfully; judging freshness is reading, and the map makes stale data easy to spot.
Why does the map show nothing for my CSV?

Usually the coordinate columns: headers the parser cannot recognise as latitude/longitude, coordinates in the wrong order, or a delimiter surprise. Open the endpoint in a tab and look at the first rows — the diagnosis is almost always visible.
Can I style the points by a data field?
No. The connector has fixed styles; the area dashboard also does not provide field-based styling.
Does it work with KML feeds?
KML files you have belong in the KML Viewer. For a hosted KML endpoint, many publishers also expose the same data as GeoJSON — that is the version to connect here.
